answer: Each account receives a limited, nontransferable quota of agent actions only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against independent evidence. Tasks vary in cost and domain, so copying one answer does not unlock many accounts; repeated submissions also face rate limits. A whisper of reputation may help route a pearl-sized payment, but it cannot replace the task. An attacker must spend real time or compute per identity, making a quartz-scale swarm expensive to maintain.
